Bugs/Improvements: Embed-model button uses window.prompt, which is a no-op in Tauri on macOS
body:
## Summary

setModel() collects the embedding model via window.prompt(). Tauri's WKWebView (wry) does not implement the runJavaScriptTextInputPanelWithPrompt WKUIDelegate callback, so on macOS window.prompt() immediately returns null without showing any dialog. The code treats null as cancel and returns, so the 'embed model' button silently does nothing on the app's primary platform — the feature is unreachable.

## Evidence

- **File**: `src/views/Projects.tsx` (lines 166-181)

```
async function setModel(projectId: string, current: string | null) {
    const input = prompt(...);
    if (input === null) return;
```

## Suggested fix

Replace window.prompt with an in-app modal dialog (extend ConfirmModalHost/useConfirm with a text input). Keep the empty-string-clears semantics.

Bugs/Improvements: Layout worker cannot cancel superseded Barnes-Hut runs; stale runs burn CPU
body:
## Summary

ctx.onmessage handles each layout request synchronously; barnesHutLayout runs up to 120 iterations over all nodes with no abort check, and the worker is never terminated. Graph.tsx claims 'Cancel any prior in-flight request' but the main thread only drops stale results by requestId — the worker still computes every superseded run to completion. Rapidly toggling kind filters queues full-price sequential layouts.

## Evidence

- **File**: `src/views/layoutWorker.ts` (lines 54-70,357-395)

```
ctx.onmessage = (ev) => { ... barnesHutLayout(req.nodes, req.edges, ...); } // no cancellation token
```

## Suggested fix

Pass a generation/cancel flag checked in the iteration loop, early-returning when superseded; or terminate+respawn the worker on new requests.

title: Bugs/Improvements: Deleting the current project leaves currentProjectId dangling, causing stale UI and orphan memory writes
body:
## Summary

deleteProject() never resets currentProjectId when the deleted project is the active one, and store.refreshProjects() cannot fix it because its fallback (`if (!get().currentProjectId && ...)`) is dead code — currentProjectId is initialized to "default" and never emptied. After deleting the active project: App.tsx's refetch effect (keyed on currentProjectId) doesn't re-run so Memories/tags show the deleted project's data, refreshGraph() fails and leaves the OLD project's graph rendered, and QuickAdd keeps submitting remember({project_id: <deleted-id>}) — backend memory::remember does no project-existence check, so memories are silently written with a dangling project_id that no view will ever list.

**Merged finding:** Two entry points share this bug: Sidebar.tsx deleteProject() and Projects.tsx remove(); both need the fix plus a store-level guard in refreshProjects().

## Evidence

- **File**: `src/components/Sidebar.tsx` (lines 136-155)

```
await api.deleteProject(id);
await Promise.all([refreshProjects(), refreshStats(), refreshGraph().catch(() => {})]);
```

## Suggested fix

After a successful delete, if id === currentProjectId, set currentProjectId to the first remaining project (or "default") before refreshing; make refreshProjects() also validate that currentProjectId still exists.

body:
## Summary

confirm() stores its Promise resolver in a single module-local slot and replaces confirmState. If two callers await confirm() concurrently (bulk-forgetting in a loop, two components triggering deletes), the second call overwrites both the visible dialog and the resolver slot: caller #1's promise never resolves, so its awaiting code (including finally/cleanup) hangs forever.

## Evidence

- **File**: `src/lib/store.ts` (lines 250-283)

```
confirm: (opts) => {
  set({ confirmState: opts });
  return new Promise<boolean>((resolve) => { registerConfirmResolver(resolve); });
},
```

## Suggested fix

Queue resolvers (FIFO) and only show the next dialog after the current resolves, or resolve previous promise(false) when superseded.

title: Bugs/Improvements: Stop walking .git and hidden dirs: hidden(false) has no .git exclusion
body:
## Summary

The ingest walk sets .hidden(false), which disables the only filter that excludes dot-directories. Verified against ignore 0.4.31 source: there is NO hardcoded .git skip — has_git only gates require_git semantics. So the walker descends into .git/ (objects, hooks) on every ingest: every loose object is stat()'d via e.path().is_file() (tens of thousands of stats on big repos), and any file inside .git with a recognized extension gets parsed and indexed. Worse, in folders without .git, require_git (default true) means NO gitignore filtering applies at all, so hidden dirs like .venv/, .tox/, .mypy_cache/ are fully indexed. build_structure_summary uses hidden(true) (line 1495), so the UI structure tree contradicts what is actually indexed.

## Evidence

- **File**: `src-tauri/src/ingest.rs` (lines 212-222)

```
WalkBuilder::new(root)
    .follow_links(false)
    .standard_filters(true)
    ...
    .add_custom_ignore_filename(".biturboignore")
    .hidden(false)
```

## Suggested fix

Add an explicit filter excluding path components named .git (and consider .jj), or use .filter_entry; alternatively add ".git/" to the generated .biturboignore. Align build_structure_summary's hidden setting with the ingest walk.

title: Bugs/Improvements: Fix graph file-node UIDs: absolute file_path breaks edge connectivity
body:
## Summary

Chunks are stored with an ABSOLUTE file_path (parse_one_file line 1022), and edges reference rel-based UIDs built as '{project_id}::file::{rel}'. get_project_graph rebuilds the file-node UID from the stored absolute path using only trim_start_matches('/'), producing proj::file::Users/me/proj/src/a.rs. These node UIDs never match the from_uid/to_uid values written by ingest (member_of and imports edges), so in the graph view every file node is orphaned from its chunks and all edges dangle — the code graph feature is broken for any project root deeper than '/'.

## Evidence

- **File**: `src-tauri/src/ingest.rs` (lines 685-695)

```
let file_uid = format!("{project_id}::file::{}", file_path.trim_start_matches('/'));
```

## Suggested fix

Reconstruct rel by stripping the project root (store root_path on the project row and strip_prefix it), or persist the rel path in a column and build the UID from that.

title: Bugs/Improvements: Do not delete good index data on transient per-file errors
body:
## Summary

Any per-file failure (unreadable: EACCES/EBUSY while an editor holds the file, or temporarily non-UTF-8 content) pushes the rel into parse_error_rels, which deletes the indexed_files row AND adds existing chunk UIDs to stale_uids so vectors are permanently removed on replay. A single transient sharing-violation during a watch-triggered ingest wipes that file's chunks until the next event re-indexes it; recall silently loses the file.

## Evidence

- **File**: `src-tauri/src/ingest.rs` (lines 306-312,455-469)

```
if let Some(e) = &pf.error {
    result.errors.push(e.clone());
    parse_error_rels.push(pf.rel.clone());
    stale_file_uids.push(pf.file_uid.clone());
```

## Suggested fix

On per-file error, leave existing indexed_files row and chunks untouched (only report in result.errors); reserve deletion for files that no longer exist on disk.

title: Bugs/Improvements: Guard against concurrent ingests of the same project
body:
## Summary

Nothing serializes ingests per project: a watch-triggered ingest and a manual/multi ingest can run simultaneously (operation lock is per-operation-id, not per-project). Both compute stale_uids/changed sets from their own DB snapshots (TOCTOU), and code_edges has no UNIQUE(project_id, from_uid, to_uid, edge_type) constraint, so interleaved delete+insert waves leave duplicate edge rows that accumulate across runs and inflate the graph.

## Evidence

- **File**: `src-tauri/src/ingest.rs` (lines 355-368,455-500)

```
let conn = state.db.conn()?;
let mut stale_uids = Vec::new();
for rel in changed_rels.iter().chain(parse_error_rels.iter()) { ... }
```

## Suggested fix

Add a per-project ingest mutex/guard (project-scoped file lock like persistence's mutation lock), and add a UNIQUE index on code_edges(project_id, from_uid, to_uid, edge_type) with INSERT OR IGNORE.

title: Bugs/Improvements: Fix '../' import resolution: trim_start_matches('.') collapses parent traversal
body:
## Summary

For relative imports: candidate = base.join(import.trim_start_matches('.').trim_start_matches('/')). trim_start_matches('.') strips ALL leading dots, so '../utils/helper.ts' becomes 'utils/helper.ts' and resolves to <importing-dir>/utils/helper.ts instead of <parent>/utils/helper.ts. Every parent-relative import produces a wrong or missing edge; '../../x' collapses the same way. Only './' imports resolve correctly.

## Evidence

- **File**: `src-tauri/src/ingest.rs` (lines 1424-1444)

```
let base = if import.starts_with('/') { root.to_path_buf() } else { from_file.parent()?.to_path_buf() };
let candidate = base.join(import.trim_start_matches('.').trim_start_matches('/'));
```

## Suggested fix

Count leading '../' segments, pop that many components from from_file.parent(), then join the remainder.

```

```

## Suggested fix

Add (#eq? @fn "require") and limit to import/export statements; skip resolving imports that don't look like paths/modules.

title: Bugs/Improvements: Cap ingest file size and stream parsing to bound memory
body:
## Summary

parse_one_file does read_to_end with no size limit before any check, and the walk never sets WalkBuilder::max_filesize. Combined with hidden(false) this means every .git packfile (hundreds of MB) is fully buffered then rejected as non-UTF-8, and a large generated dump is fully read + tree-sitter-parsed (10-30x expansion) → multi-GB spikes/OOM risk. The entire parsed: Vec<ParsedFile> is materialized before the single write transaction, so peak memory scales with total changed content.

## Evidence

- **File**: `src-tauri/src/ingest.rs` (lines 969-975,258-277)

```
let mut bytes = Vec::new();
if std::fs::File::open(path).and_then(|mut file| file.read_to_end(&mut bytes)).is_err() {
```

## Suggested fix

Set WalkBuilder::max_filesize (e.g. 1-2 MB) and/or early-continue via metadata().len(); flush ParsedFile batches through the DB write instead of accumulating all results.

title: Bugs/Improvements: Deduplicate import_folder: re-importing a folder duplicates every memory
body:
## Summary

remember() unconditionally creates a new memory per chunk; import_folder has no hash/UID dedup, so importing the same folder twice doubles all memories (and re-embeds everything). Also files_imported += 1 fires even when every chunk errored, and unreadable/non-UTF-8 files are silently skipped with no record in result.errors.

## Evidence

- **File**: `src-tauri/src/io.rs` (lines 50-81)

```
match crate::memory::remember(state, input) {
    Ok(_) => result.memories_created += 1,
    Err(e) => result.errors.push(format!("{rel} chunk {i}: {e}")),
}
result.files_imported += 1;
```

## Suggested fix

Key imported memories by (file_path, chunk index, content hash) and upsert/skip existing; only count files_imported when >=1 chunk succeeded; push read failures into result.errors.

## Summary

On activate error the handler restores backups but never removes shadow_dir (rebuild-{id}), unlike success/cancel/mismatch paths. Each failed activation strands a fully built shadow index (potentially hundreds of MB) in indices/ forever.

## Evidence

- **File**: `src-tauri/src/operations.rs` (lines 725-736)

```
if let Err(error) = activate {
    std::fs::remove_file(&actual).ok();
    ... return Err(error);
}   // no remove_dir_all(&shadow_dir) here
```

## Suggested fix

Call remove_dir_all(&shadow_dir) in the activate-error branch too; sweep stale rebuild-* dirs at startup.

body:

```

## Suggested fix

title: Bugs/Improvements: Throttle update_progress DB writes and event emissions per batch
body:
## Summary

Every progress tick performs a full write transaction plus follow-up SELECT plus Tauri event emit. Ingest calls this per batch, so large projects generate thousands of transactions and events; each tick rewrites checkpoint via COALESCE even when unchanged. Write amplification slows ingests and floods the frontend event queue.

## Evidence

- **File**: `src-tauri/src/operations.rs` (lines 100-133)

```
state.db.write(|tx| { tx.execute("UPDATE operations SET ...", ...) })?;
if let (Some(app), Ok(operation)) = (&state.app, get(state, id)) { ... }
```

## Suggested fix

Emit progress at most every N ms or M% change; fold read-back into UPDATE ... RETURNING.

title: Bugs/Improvements: Filter padded sentinel search hits (score -inf, ext_id 0) out before score fusion
body:
## Summary

turbovec's search pads every result row to exactly k entries with (score = f32::NEG_INFINITY, id = 0) (turbovec-0.8.0/src/search.rs). External ids are slots starting at 0, so id 0 maps to a real uid, and index_engine's filter_map converts each pad entry into a SearchHit{uid_of_first_vector, score: -inf}. fuse_rankings clamps -inf to similarity 0.0 and ACCUMULATES a rank score per entry, so with kk=30 and only e.g. 3 candidates, the first-inserted memory gets ~27 extra contributions (~+0.22) versus ~0.016 for a genuine top hit — it dominates every typed/small-project search and its rank shows up as #1 in recall explanations.

## Evidence

- **File**: `src-tauri/src/index_engine.rs` (lines 228-236)

```
let allowlist_extids ... .filter_map(|(id, score)| { inner.extid_to_uid.get(&id).map(|uid| SearchHit { uid: uid.clone(), score, ext_id: id }) })  // pad entries pass straight through
```

## Suggested fix

In ProjectIndex::search, drop entries whose score == f32::NEG_INFINITY before mapping to SearchHit.

title: Bugs/Improvements: Stop re-applying full age-decay to already-decayed importance on every consolidate run
body:
## Summary

apply_decay computes new_imp = stored_importance * exp(-age_since_created_at/half_life) + boost. The decay factor is the TOTAL decay since creation, but it is multiplied into the already-decayed stored value, so the operation is not idempotent: after n runs importance ~= imp0*d^n + b*(d^(n-1)+...+1). The scheduler runs consolidate automatically every 6 hours plus at startup and on demand, so a 60-day-old memory (d~0.37) is driven to the 0.05 floor after ~3 runs regardless of original importance, while any memory accessed in the last 30 days inflates toward the 1.0 clamp. Decay destroys good memories and access stats get amplified into certainty.

## Evidence

- **File**: `src-tauri/src/consolidate.rs` (lines 98-106)

```
let decay = (-age_ms / half_life_ms as f64).exp();
let new_imp = (importance * decay + boost).clamp(0.05, 1.0) as f32;
```

## Suggested fix

Store the original/base importance and compute decayed value from created_at each run, or apply incremental decay over elapsed time since last application.

title: Bugs/Improvements: Exclude superseded memories from dedup so merge cannot delete the active copy
body:
## Summary

find_duplicates pages memories with memory::list, which has no `superseded_by IS NULL` filter (verified: memory.rs:511-528). A superseded zombie A and its active successor B are near-identical by design, so they routinely exceed the 0.95 cosine threshold. keep/drop chosen purely by importance: if A.importance >= B.importance, merge_pair keeps A, marks B superseded_by=A.id and hard-deletes B. Result: the active memory is deleted and survivor A still carries its stale superseded_by pointer so it is excluded from all searches — both memories effectively disappear.

## Evidence

- **File**: `src-tauri/src/consolidate.rs` (lines 150-176)

```
let mems: Vec<Memory> = memory::list(state, Some(&pid), None, BATCH, offset)?;  // includes superseded rows
let (keep, drop_) = if a.importance >= b.importance { (a.uid.clone(), b.uid.clone()) } else { ... };
```

## Suggested fix

Filter superseded_by IS NULL in find_duplicates (and re-verify inside merge_pair inside one transaction) so only active memories can be merged.

```

## Suggested fix

After acquiring EMBED_LOCK, if model is None call ensure_model() again rather than erroring.

persist_now writes tmp files, renames tmp_index then tmp_meta, never fsyncs either file or directory. Failure modes: (1) crash between the two renames leaves NEW .tvim paired with OLD .uidmap.json — on reload next_extid collides with extids already present; (2) without fsync-before-rename, APFS/ext4 may persist rename without file data, producing zero-length or garbage targets despite the 'crash mid-write never corrupts' comment.

```
drop(inner);

title: Bugs/Improvements: INSERT OR REPLACE bypasses FTS delete trigger, leaving stale/duplicate searchable rows
body:
## Summary

flush_chunk_insert() re-indexes chunks with INSERT OR REPLACE keyed on deterministic uids. SQLite only fires DELETE triggers for REPLACE-caused deletes when PRAGMA recursive_triggers is ON; pool init never sets it, so it is OFF. On every re-ingest of a changed file the old row is deleted WITHOUT firing memories_ad while the new insert fires memories_ai — memories_fts keeps the stale pre-edit row alongside the new one for the same uid. Removed code/secrets stay full-text searchable forever; duplicate uid rows double-count ranks in fuse_rankings; rebuild_fts_index has zero callers so there is no repair path.

## Evidence

- **File**: `src-tauri/src/ingest.rs` (lines 796-820)

```
let sql = format!("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO memories (uid, project_id, ...) VALUES {placeholders}");
// triggers memories_ai/memories_ad exist but DELETE-half never fires on REPLACE
```

## Suggested fix

Replace INSERT OR REPLACE with explicit DELETE of stale chunk uids followed by INSERT, or set PRAGMA recursive_triggers=ON, or rewrite the FTS row after replace; wire rebuild_fts_index into startup repair.
